correctness.rationale: A complete bijection maps words in the exact Parikh class to bounded partitions of area C. Distinct earlier/later a choices give abbab iff two positive parts differ by at least two. Hence avoidance forces positive parts to have spread at most one, and for every feasible positive-part count there is exactly one balanced partition. This proves the count, total polynomial, sharp maximum, universal avoidability and probability for all nonnegative parameters with 0<=C<=AB. Independently executed brute-force 48,619 words/1,377 fibers and automaton 6,253 fibers reproduce exact counts and denominator. Finite computations are not used to prove arbitrary-parameter steps.

Thus the known sandwich-pattern count is a lower bound for this distinct avoidance event, not its exact enumeration.

value.rationale: The 2026 fixed-Parikh-class probability problem requests quantitative fixed-pattern frequencies, but its general result is only additive approximation and several shorter pattern cases have different arithmetic complexity. The all-parameter closed inversion-refined count for a natural five-letter scattered pattern has a substantive structural positive-part-spread characterization, proves every class has an avoider, yields the complete generating polynomial and a sharp max. The numerator admits a direct constant-number-of-arithmetic-operations formula even though the Gaussian denominator can be large. It is not a mere single numerical instance or an unmotivated slice.
